findings.claim: The copy constructor MessagePackSecurity(MessagePackSecurity copyFrom) no longer copies HashCollisionResistant. Any options derived via WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth or similar clone paths silently drop collision resistance and revert to the default. That is a security regression and a behavior change for existing users, and it is unrelated to the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Create MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData (HashCollisionResistant=true), call WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(10) or use the copy ctor via a derived class, and assert HashCollisionResistant is still true. Base passes, head fails. Also run the existing MessagePackSecurityTests.

findings.claim: The attribute is wrapped in #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK. A consumer targeting netstandard2.1, or netstandard2.0 plus netcoreapp, behaves as intended. A consumer targeting only netstandard2.0 or net4x still gets no exclusion, so 'all generated code decorated' is not met on those TFMs. ExcludeFromCodeCoverage exists in netstandard2.0 and net45+, so the guard is unnecessarily restrictive. Generated output also now differs per TFM.

receipt_plan.detail: ExcludeFromCodeCoverage is available in netstandard2.0 (System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis) and .NET Framework 4.0+. Compile a generated formatter against netstandard2.0 without the #if to confirm it builds; the guard then needlessly skips these TFMs.

findings.claim: The TransformUtilities change from "{" to "{\r\n" for nesting types with constraints alters the generated text for every nested generic type with constraints, so users' checked-in or snapshotted generator output changes. It is a formatting-only change outside the requirement. It is harmless for compilation, but it adds snapshot churn.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the generator snapshot tests, including the nested-generic-with-constraints cases, and diff the generated files against base to find output that changed beyond the attribute.

findings.claim: A #if/#endif block is placed directly before a type declaration after the nesting-type output. The StringKey, Formatter and Union templates emit the preprocessor directive at the start of a line right after the previous write, with no guaranteed leading newline. With the TransformUtilities newline fix this is probably fine. If a previous write does not end in a newline, the '#if' will not be at line start and the generated code will fail to compile.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the snapshot and compile tests for nested non-generic, nested generic with constraints, and global-namespace types for StringKey, Formatter and Union templates, and check that '#if' begins a line in each.
